newsitem.title: UK: UK confident about chances of reforming EU's CAP.
newsitem.headline: UK confident about chances of reforming EU's CAP.

text.p: Britain's new government is confident it can help reform the European Union's controversial and costly Common Agricultural Policy, Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said.

The Labour party, which won a landslide election victory on May 1, promised to reform the CAP, which supports EU farm prices by limiting production and buying up surpluses but is denounced by critics as highly inefficient.
"It won't be easy or immediate, but I am sure that over time we can be tougher on the waste of the CAP," Cook told journalists.
He said there were three reasons to be confident that the CAP could be reformed:
-- Realisation within the EU that member states would not allow the overall cost of running the CAP -- which is gradually falling --- to rise again
-- The fact that the CAP could not be extended in its current form to the next tier of states applying to become members of the European Union because it would be too expensive
-- International pressure and the trend towards global free trade would force the EU to change what Cook said was a protectionist policy.
A British ministry of agriculture memorandum released last month said the EU had paid cereal farmers sums worth $19 billion too much in compensation.
